item.title: Pangu Highway links communities across PNG
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape says his decision to travel by road from Port Moresby through Gulf, Lae, Goroka, Simbu, Jiwaka and into Mt Hagen was deliberate-to see first hand how infrastructure is connecting the country and to challenge Papua New Guineans to become more productive. item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape says his decision to travel by road from Port Moresby through Gulf, Lae, Goroka, Simbu, Jiwaka and into Mt Hagen was deliberate-to see first hand how infrastructure is connecting the country and to challenge Papua New Guineans to become more productive.

Arriving in Mt Hagen on Thursday evening with his convoy, Mr Marape said the journey along the newly cut Pangu Highway comes as the country prepares to celebrate its 51st Independence Day on September 16.

“We are seven days away from Independence, and this country must be united through infrastructure. National unity must be seen through the roads that connect our people,” Marape said.

He said the journey was also meant to show that every Papua New Guinean has a role in building the country's future.

“Everyone in this country must be productive. We must work and contribute so that we can build this country together as one,” he said.

Marape said travelling along the newly cut road also gave him and his team an opportunity to see first-hand how government funding, decisions and development efforts are being translated into infrastructure on the ground.

“We have made the decisions, we have provided the funding and we have put the effort into these roads. We also need to come and see for ourselves how that investment is being put to good use,” the Prime Minister said.

He said physically travelling the route gave him a clearer understanding of the condition of the roads, the progress of infrastructure and the challenges faced by communities.

The Prime Minister also strongly encouraged Papua New Guineans to work hard, utilise their land and make productive use of their time.

“Work hard. Toil your land. Make good use of your land and your time. You have to participate in the economy so that other people, especially those in remote areas, can also benefit from services,” Marape stressed.

The prime minister said national development could not depend entirely on the government.

“Government cannot do everything. Our people also have to participate in commercial activity on their land,” he stated.

Mr Marape encouraged people from the Highlands to the coastal areas to produce commodities such as coffee, cocoa, copra, and other agricultural products.

“Plant coffee, plant cocoa, produce copra and other commodities. The government has markets and will continue to assist with markets, but our people must produce,” he encouraged.

He said PNG has the potential to collectively help the government repay debts taken to develop roads, infrastructure and public services if people actively participate in the economy.

“If every person, from the Highlands to the coast, participates in commercial activity, we can collectively help our government to repay the debts taken to build these services and infrastructure,” Mr. Marape said.

He stressed that the ultimate objective was to ensure that development and economic opportunities reach people even in remote areas.

“When our people participate in the economy, we can create more opportunities for services to reach everyone, including our people in the remote areas,” he said.

As Papua New Guinea prepares to mark its 51st Independence anniversary, the prime minister's message is that roads alone will not develop the country - Papua New Guineans must use those roads, their land and their resources to produce, trade and grow the national economy.

item.title: John Rosso’s long road journey
item.description: At 2am Sunday, 6th of September 2026, Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso was on the road. He was travelling with Prime Minister James Marape and the government delegation on the long journey towards Lae.
item.content:encoded:
At 2am Sunday, 6th of September 2026, Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso was on the road.

He was travelling with Prime Minister James Marape and the government delegation on the long journey towards Lae.

For Rosso, it was more than a trip to attend an official opening. It was a chance to experience the road and see the communities along the way.

The journey took the convoy through towns, villages and remote areas. Along the road, people came out to welcome them. Some stopped the vehicles and offered bananas, pineapples, coconuts, betel nut and food.

Rosso noticed something simple. Many of the people did not have much. But they still gave what they had. That stayed with him.

The long journey also reminded Rosso why the Connect PNG programme matters. For people in remote communities, a road is not just a road. It is a way to reach a school. A way to reach a hospital. A way to take food and crops to market.

Rosso spoke about communities where people still walk for days to reach basic services. He said every Papua New Guinean deserved better access, no matter where they lived.

“The opinion of the person that lives in a remote society, that wants that road, matters,” he said.

The journey also gave Rosso a closer look at the size of the country and the distances many people travel every day.

For those living in Port Moresby or Lae, a long road trip may be unusual. For people in remote communities, it is part of everyday life. Rosso said criticism of government projects would always come.

“You can never please everyone,” he said.

But he said the government must continue working to connect people. The Pangu Highway, being developed under Connect PNG, is part of that effort to improve the road link between Port Moresby and Lae and connect communities along the way.

For Rosso, the most powerful part of the journey was not the kilometres covered. It was the people waiting beside the road. They waved. They shared food. They welcomed the convoy. And they showed him why better roads matter.

After travelling through the night and into the day, Rosso arrived in Lae. But the journey had already given him something the opening ceremony could not. A firsthand reminder that for many Papua New Guineans, a road is a connection to a better life.

item.title: Three-day alcohol ban for Central
item.description: A three-day total restriction on the sale, purchase, and public consumption of alcohol will be enforced across Central during the 51st Independence Day anniversary celebrations this month. The liquor ban will take effect on Tuesday, Sept 15, and run through to Thursday, Sept 17. Independence Day falls on Wednesday, Sept 16.
item.content:encoded:
A three-day total restriction on the sale, purchase, and public consumption of alcohol will be enforced across Central during the 51st Independence Day anniversary celebrations this month.

The liquor ban will take effect on Tuesday, Sept 15, and run through to Thursday, Sept 17. Independence Day falls on Wednesday, Sept 16.

Acting Provincial Administrator and Chief Liquor Commissioner Bala Kapa authorized the restriction to ensure public safety, preserve order, and protect the dignity of the national event.

"This measure has been implemented to ensure public safety, maintain order, and uphold the dignity of our celebrations," Kapa said in an official notice.

He urged residents across the province to celebrate and participate in the scheduled festivities responsibly.

Police units will conduct regular patrols across all districts, while inspectors from the Central Provincial Liquor Licensing Authority will maintain strict surveillance to monitor compliance.

Major commercial hospitality operations have been exempted from the order. Establishments permitted to continue normal operations include; hotels, motels, lodges, taverns, publican bars and Resorts.

All non-exempt businesses, including bottle shops and trade stores, must remain closed to alcohol sales for the duration of the period.

item.title: Undialu: Hela law and order is provincial and national importance
item.description: Hela governor Philip Undialu says law and order in the province is a matter of both provincial and national importance, particularly as Hela is host to the PNG LNG project. Undialu said this in light of the Hela Provincial Assembly and Provincial Executive Council [PEC], having considered the recent ex parte Supreme Court stay order affecting the National Court proceedings on law and order in Hela
item.content:encoded:
Hela governor Philip Undialu says law and order in the province is a matter of both provincial and national importance, particularly as Hela is host to the PNG LNG project.

Undialu said this in light of the Hela Provincial Assembly and Provincial Executive Council [PEC], having considered the recent ex parte Supreme Court stay order affecting the National Court proceedings on law and order in Hela, resolved as follows:

The Hela Provincial Government and Provincial Administrator are named respondents but were neither consulted nor consented to the application for the stay. We have been preparing to appear before the Resident Judge and provide evidence on the work being undertaken to address law and order.

"We reaffirm our full support for the Resident Judge and the National Court’s work in Hela. Law and justice are fundamental to the protection of our people and their rights, and the Resident Court provides an important avenue to examine these challenges and find lasting solutions."

"We respectfully call on Solicitor General Joseph Aka to withdraw or seek the discharge of the ex parte stay so that the substantive National Court proceedings can proceed.

"The summonses and directions were issued on June 2026. The Prime Minister is expected to participate on 12 September, and I am scheduled to participate on 17 September," he said.

He stressed that the Commissioner of Police and Commissioner of Correctional Services have important constitutional and statutory responsibilities to protect lives, maintain public safety and uphold law and order.

He said law and order is fundamentally a human-rights issue.

Governor Undialu emphasized that when people’s lives and property are at risk, every responsible institution must be prepared to account for what it has done and what more it will do.

He said if national agencies believe Hela’s law-and-justice capacity is inadequate, then come before the court, provide the evidence, explain the gaps and tell the people what additional support and action will be provided.

"We should be man enough to face the questions and guarantee that we will do better, rather than allowing court processes to become a means of avoiding scrutiny or accountability.

"If the stay is not withdrawn or discharged, the Hela provincial government will immediately take appropriate legal steps to object to and challenge it before the Supreme Court, in accordance with the law," he stated.

The governor said Hela hosts the PNG LNG project, generating billions of kina in economic activity. Law and order in Hela is therefore a matter of both provincial and national importance.

"We respect the independence of the courts and will not prejudge matters before them.

"Let the evidence be heard. Let every summoned person be heard. Let those responsible account for their constitutional responsibilities. Let the courts determine the issues according to law," governor Undialu said.

item.title: Ramu Nickel LOs demand legacy issues resolved before expansion and CDA talks
item.description: The four principal Landowners Associations [LOAs] of the Chinese-operated Ramu Nickel and Cobalt project in Madang Province have jointly resolved not to participate in the proposed Community Development Agreement [CDA] negotiations, scheduled for Lae later this month, unless critical outstanding issues affecting the existing project are properly addressed. The landowners explained in a joint press
item.content:encoded:
The four principal Landowners Associations [LOAs] of the Chinese-operated Ramu Nickel and Cobalt project in Madang Province have jointly resolved not to participate in the proposed Community Development Agreement [CDA] negotiations, scheduled for Lae later this month, unless critical outstanding issues affecting the existing project are properly addressed.

The landowners explained in a joint press statement issued over the weekend that their decision does not oppose the project or any further developments, rather a protest against proceeding with negotiations for a new CDA, whilst fundamental questions concerning historical royalties, compensation, relocation, employment, business opportunities, environmental and social impacts remain unresolved.

They demand that the royalty payments from 2013-2025 must be verified.

The four LOA chairmen, Steven Saud for Coastal Pipeline, Yavina Kassima [Maigari], Kuai Dup [Basamuk], and John Tigavu, vice chairman for Kurumbukari, released the signed statement, raising their immediate concern is whether the royalties paid to customary landowners from the commencement of commercial production in 2013 through to 2025 were correctly calculated.

The company has previously explained that its royalty methodology includes the use of Net Smelter Returns [NSR] for Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate [MHP] and Free on Board [FOB] revenue for chromium concentrate, together with deductions associated with refinery and processing operations.

However, the landowners believe a transparent reconciliation is necessary to establish whether the amounts paid were in fact the amounts legally and contractually payable.

They are demanding that an independent royalty audit covering 2013 to 2025 be conducted to examine production and sales records, product valuation, royalty rates methodology, NSR and FOB calculations, all deductions and the actual royalties calculated, paid and distributed.

"If the royalties are correct, let the records and an independent audit prove it. If there has been a shortfall, let the audit establish the amount and let the outstanding royalties be paid," the landowners said in a statement.

They added that the immediate issue is whether the customary landowners have received the correct royalties under the existing Ramu Nickel Project arrangements or not.

The landowners further stated that they do not accept that their participation in a future CDA negotiation should automatically mean acceptance of historical royalty payments as full and final settlement.

Meanwhile, other issues they have also raised include outstanding compensation and relocation, fair employment, and business opportunities, plus environmental and community concerns.

The four LOAs maintain that all outstanding compensation and relocation issues associated with the existing project must be addressed before any further expansion can proceed.

They are also concerned about the unequal distribution of employment and project- related business opportunities amongst the four LOAs.

They want the proposed expansion to establish a transparent and equitable framework for landowner participation.

The landowners continue to raise concerns about environmental and social impacts associated with the existing operation, particularly around Basamuk and Kurumbukari.

These include concerns about accumulated waste materials, emissions, fumes, dust and noise, as well as the need for a comprehensive environmental, health and demographic assessments across the project footprint.

The four LOAs are calling upon Ramu NiCo Management [MCC] Limited and the National Government to immediately establish a joint mechanism involving them to address these outstanding matters.

item.title: UFL reaffirms customer commitment with nationwide independence draw
item.description: United Finance Limited [UFL] has awarded K51,000 in cash prizes to 81 customers across Papua New Guinea to mark the nation’s Independence anniversary. The nationwide Independence Cash Giveaway Promotion concluded with an official random draw conducted at the institution’s headquarters, where eligible clients were selected for cash rewards.
item.content:encoded:
United Finance Limited [UFL] has awarded K51,000 in cash prizes to 81 customers across Papua New Guinea to mark the nation’s Independence anniversary.

The nationwide Independence Cash Giveaway Promotion concluded with an official random draw conducted at the institution’s headquarters, where eligible clients were selected for cash rewards.

Under the prize distribution; 21 winners each received K1000 while 60 others got K500 each.

During the event, Client Retention and Compliance Team Leader Lavenda Konga drew the lucky winners for the Momase region.

UFL Group Media and Marketing Manager Hinuvi Onafimo said the promotion was designed to celebrate PNG’s independence while appreciating customer loyalty.

“As Papua New Guinea prepares to celebrate another year of independence, we are delighted to share this occasion with our customers,” Onafimo said.

“The promotion is our way of thanking our customers for their loyalty and support. We congratulate all the winners and encourage our customers to continue banking with confidence through United Finance.”

Onafimo said the high participation rate demonstrated growing confidence in UFL’s financial services.

He added that the company remains committed to providing accessible financial products for individuals, families, and businesses nationwide.

item.title: Middle Ramu MP devastated by plane crash
item.description: The Member for Middle Ramu, Kansol Kamdaru, says he is devastated over yesterday's tragic plane crash in his remote district, which claimed the lives of three people. The light aircraft operated by Niugini Aviation, was under the command of pilot Paul Gueme and his two passengers, had departed Mt Hagen soon after 1pm yesterday on a chartered run but met its fate about six miles south of Simbai.
item.content:encoded:
The Member for Middle Ramu, Kansol Kamdaru, says he is devastated over yesterday's tragic plane crash in his remote district, which claimed the lives of three people.

The light aircraft operated by Niugini Aviation, was under the command of pilot Paul Gueme and his two passengers, had departed Mt Hagen soon after 1pm yesterday on a chartered run but met its fate about six miles south of Simbai.

"I am so devastated to hear about the plane crash in my district. My people rely heavily on these third level aircrafts for their transportation needs, and what happened yesterday is a great loss to my district and my people," Kamdaru said.

"I also wish to express heartfelt condolences on behalf of my district and my people to the families and relatives of the three men who perished in the unfortunate incident. Our thoughts and prayers are with you all at this difficult time.

"Your loss is our loss too. Niugini Aviation has played a tremendous part in the lives of my people and contributed immensely to the development of Middle Ramu."

Former Madang Governor, Jim Kas, who is also a local man from Simbai, said Papua New Guinea has lost a great man, a very well experienced pilot, who did his job diligently, not for money but for the love of flying and contributing to the development of the remotest parts of this country.

"I have known the late pilot for a long time," Kas said.

"Knowing Paul, he loves flying and had the gist for the most difficult tasks. He understood the small people well and their needs, despite bad weather conditions, rugged terrains, and the remoteness of places. He took risks and flew across Papua New Guinea.

"He found happiness, satisfaction in serving the remote people. He knew the beauty of landing a plane in remote areas and seeing people smile when they see a plane land because that is their only connection to the outside world. Paul was the man in between, and he delivered it until yeaterday," Mr Kas said.

He also said that late Gueme flew in to Simbai three to four times a day until yesterday when he met his fate.

As a former leader for Madang, Kas also expressed sadness on his passing, as well as the two passengers.

"On behalf of the people of Middle Ramu, Raikos, and other remote areas of Madang Province that rely mostly on small aircrafts for their transportation needs, I would like to extend our deepest condolences to Paul's family, and the families of the two passengers who died in the tragic crash yesterday afternoon," he said.

item.title: 2 police officers among three arrested over jailbreak
item.description: Two Police officers and a civilian have been arrested and charged for assisting in the recent mass jail break of 25 prisoners at the Wabag Police Station in Enga. Acting Provincial Police Commander Chief Inspector Daniel Yangen said the officers have been arrested and charged with 22 indictable offences which includes aiding and abetting of the escapees. While the civilian was charged with aiding
item.content:encoded:
Two Police officers and a civilian have been arrested and charged for assisting in the recent mass jail break of 25 prisoners at the Wabag Police Station in Enga.

Acting Provincial Police Commander Chief Inspector Daniel Yangen said the officers have been arrested and charged with 22 indictable offences which includes aiding and abetting of the escapees. While the civilian was charged with aiding an escapee.

The three arrested were locked up at the Wabag Police Station without bail as they await court proceedings.

Chief Inspector Yangen has given orders to police prosecutors to produce the report on the prison escape. Meanwhile, the civilian is awaiting appropriate charges to be laid by police.

While that is going on Acting PPC Yangen has started awareness to apprehend the escapees, starting in Tsak Valley and at the Wapenamanda area.

He said it is important for the rule of law to take place whilst reminding leaders, magistrates and community members that they will be charged and arrested if found harboring and aiding these escapees and preventing justice to take its course.

The awareness follows an investigation on the issue by Internal Affairs.

So far, no prisoner of the 25 who escaped has been caught yet.
